name: Miami
tagline: Cold crab since 1913, and the café con leche that Versailles never stops pouring.

Joe's Stone Crab.description: The cold stone crab claws with mustard sauce that have defined Miami since 1913. Open only November through May.

Versailles.description: The heart of Cuban cuisine in Miami, with a ballroom and café con leche flowing around the clock.

Le Jardinier.description: Vegetable-forward French cuisine in the Design District, with a Michelin star in Florida's debut guide.

Ariete.description: Contemporary American technique with Cuban roots from chef Michael Beltran in Coconut Grove. Michelin star.

Los Pinareños Fruteria.description: A family-run fruit stand in Little Havana since 1963, famous for its freshly pressed guarapo (sugarcane juice).

Mac's Club Deuce.description: Miami Beach's oldest bar, an unfiltered dive since 1926. Anthony Bourdain visited it on three different shows and called it one of his favorite places on Earth.

Michael's Genuine Food & Drink.description: Market-driven American cooking from James Beard-winning chef Michael Schwartz in the Design District. Bourdain called it "probably the best restaurant in Miami right now" on The Layover.

Yardbird Southern Table & Bar.description: Southern fried chicken brined for 27 hours that Anthony Bourdain sampled on his Miami visit. James Beard-nominated for Best New Restaurant.

Islas Canarias.description: Cuban bakery and restaurant famous for croquetas widely voted among Miami's best. Anthony Bourdain visited with chef Michelle Bernstein on Parts Unknown.

Mandolin Aegean Bistro.description: Flavors of Greece and Turkey in a restored bungalow in the Design District, holding a Michelin Bib Gourmand since 2022.

Boia De.description: Neighborhood Italian cooking with American touches in a tiny Little Haiti storefront. One Michelin star for chefs Luciana Giangrandi and Alex Meyer.

Fiola Miami.description: Refined Italian cuisine from James Beard Award-winning, Michelin-starred chef Fabio Trabocchi, now in Coral Gables.

Prime 112.description: The South Beach steakhouse where celebrities have gathered since 2004, consistently ranked among the highest-grossing restaurants in the U.S.

Garcia's Seafood Grille & Fish Market.description: Family-run seafood spot on the Miami River, founded in 1966 by exiled Cuban brothers who started out as fishmongers.

Puerto Sagua.description: South Beach Cuban diner since 1962, with ties to the original Puerto Sagua in Havana. The Cuban sandwich and ropa vieja never disappoint.

La Sandwicherie.description: Open-air French sandwich counter in South Beach since 1988, open until 5 a.m.

El Palacio de los Jugos.description: Cuban market-cafeteria hybrid open for more than 40 years, famous for its fresh-pressed tropical juices and roast pork.

Havana Harry's.description: Family-style Cuban cooking in Coral Gables since 1995, with a Michelin Guide mention and a cult-favorite Cuban sandwich.

Azucar Ice Cream Company.description: Artisanal Little Havana ice cream shop since 2011, known for flavors like flan and Abuela Maria (vanilla with guava and Maria cookies).

Panther Coffee.description: Pioneering specialty coffee roaster in Wynwood since 2010, one of the first to bring third-wave coffee culture to Miami.

Zak the Baker.description: Kosher Wynwood bakery famous for its sourdough and challah, voted Miami's best bakery.

Andiamo Brick Oven Pizza.description: Wood-fired pizzeria in the historic MiMo District since 2001, with outdoor picnic tables and dough made fresh daily.

Broken Shaker.description: The cocktail bar at Miami Beach's Freehand hotel, twice James Beard-nominated and named among the World's 50 Best Bars.

Stubborn Seed.description: A bold tasting menu from Top Chef winner Jeremy Ford, Michelin-starred since Florida's inaugural guide.

Coyo Taco.description: Wynwood taqueria making up to 1,000 handmade tortillas a day, open until 3 a.m.

News Cafe.description: 24-hour Ocean Drive café since 1988, where Gianni Versace had breakfast before he was murdered outside his mansion in 1997.

Sanguich de Miami.description: The Cuban sandwich spot that started as a shipping container in 2017 and now holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand five years running.

La Camaronera.description: Cuban seafood counter in Little Havana since 1973, founded by the García brothers. Famous for its pan con minuta.

Bachour.description: Pastry chef Antonio Bachour's workshop in Coral Gables, one of only three bakeries in the U.S. with a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

Pincho.description: Burger and pincho chain born in Miami in 2010, with Latin American flavors like vaca frita.
